summary: A real wedge (private family input for seating conflicts), but evidence is forum anecdotes only, it is a one-time $19 purchase against free tools, and 'text Mom' is the likely status quo. Seasonal timing and no founder fit make it not worth a test slot.

demand.evidence: WeddingWire threads show seating drama, but no prevalence data and no one asking for a tool; paid solvers exist ($19-$29) but do not prove demand for the contributor-link wedge.

statusQuo.evidence: Sticky notes, spreadsheets, free Zola/Seatbee, and a call or text to the parents; cheap and probably good enough.

specificity.evidence: Buyer is an engaged couple with 80-200 guests; a category, nobody spoken to, and no founder fit in David's interests.

wedge.evidence: Contributor links, not the solver, are the differentiator; a free-2-links / $19 unlock is sound, but the wedge is a token form that is easy to copy.

futureFit.evidence: One-time, low-frequency purchase with no retention; AI makes solvers a commodity and free tools improve.

premises: Conflict knowledge sits with parents and the wedding party — plausible, unmeasured.
Couples will send a link rather than text or call — unsupported.
Family members will honestly submit keep-apart notes in writing — unsupported.
Couples will pay $19 despite free Seatbee/Zola — weakly supported.
Search can reach buyers in the 3-6 week window — plausible but crowded and seasonal.
alternatives: Solver-only static page, free: fastest, no wedge, competes directly with free tools.
Contributor-link MVP per the PRD: tests the wedge, medium effort, low demand evidence.
Lateral: a family-input form only that exports a conflict list to the couple's existing tool; smallest build, tests the real hypothesis, hard to charge for.
No existing David repo covers weddings or seating; the pettycourt and squadwrap ideas share the friend-submitted-links pattern but are not code.
wedge: A fake-door flow: add guests, generate 1-3 private contributor links, see who flagged whom; no solver, PDF or payment yet.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel, Turso free, TypeScript hill-climb solver. M1 as written is only the solver, which does not test the wedge. Proving test: 150 guests, 30 pair rules, 15 tables of 10, zero must-avoid violations in under 2 seconds.

risks: Free anchors (Seatbee, Zola) cap the price
Seasonality: May-Oct weddings, 3-6 week buying window, and it is late October
Sensitive family-feud data needs deletion and strict isolation
Contributors may refuse to write down conflicts
Competitor details are from unverified marketplace listings
killCriteria: After two weeks, fewer than 3 waitlist signups from 50+ visitors, or nobody reaches the link-generation step; couples say they would just text their parents; or Zola/Seatbee add contributor input.
